gist: A new Taschen book compiles dance-themed photographs from the historic Life magazine archive.
The images chronicle shifts in American culture, gender politics, race relations and individualism.
Featured moments include Cold War tensions, iconic performers, high school proms and global dance crazes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Taschen published LIFE. Let’s Dance, a book drawing on dance photography from the archive of Life magazine, which ran weekly between 1936 and 1972. The collection covers social dancing across ballrooms, clubs, proms and parties, showcasing styles from the waltz and lindy hop to the twist. It also documents renowned performers, including George Balanchine, Margot Fonteyn, Rudolf Nureyev, Whitey’s Lindy Hoppers, the Rockettes, and actors filming the movie musical Can-Can.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The archive reflects broader shifts in twentieth-century American society. The transition from structured couple dancing to freeform movement captured emerging gender politics and individualism. Photographs also traced shifting racial dynamics, from segregated venues and newly desegregated schools to the mainstream adoption of Black and Latin American styles. In addition, dance intersected with Cold War tensions, from Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev criticising Hollywood routines to comparisons between American and Soviet schools.
